title: Door to Hell
brief: A natural-gas crater burning continuously since 1971.
story: Soviet geologists drilled a methane cavern in 1971. The ground collapsed. They set it alight to burn off the gas — thinking it would last weeks. Five decades later, the Door to Hell still burns, visible from orbit on clear nights.

title: Blood Falls
brief: Iron-rich saltwater, trapped for 1.5 million years, bleeds crimson out of a glacier.
story: A subglacial lake, sealed since the Pliocene, leaks through cracks. The brine meets oxygen at the surface and oxidises instantly — rusting into a vivid blood-red cascade across the Taylor Glacier.

title: Catatumbo Lightning
brief: Up to 300 lightning-filled nights a year, 28 flashes per minute at its peak.
story: Warm Caribbean air hits the cold Andes above Lake Maracaibo. The collision spawns the most intense sustained lightning storm on Earth — so reliable that sailors used it as a lighthouse for centuries.

title: Sailing Stones
brief: Rocks that move across a dry lakebed on their own, leaving perfect trails.
story: For a century, no one saw them move. Time-lapse GPS finally caught it: a thin winter sheet of water freezes overnight, floats the rocks on an ice raft, and a light breeze pushes them metres across the playa.

title: Roopkund — Skeleton Lake
brief: A glacial lake at 5,029 m holding 800+ ancient skeletons.
story: Melting ice reveals the dead each summer. DNA analysis shows three unrelated groups across 1,000 years — South Asians from 800 CE, Mediterraneans from 1800 CE, Southeast Asians more recently. The cause of death: cricket-ball-sized hailstones, fractures above the skull. A pilgrimage gone catastrophic.

title: Bioluminescent Bay
brief: The brightest bioluminescent bay on Earth — every ripple glows electric blue.
story: Dinoflagellates (Pyrodinium bahamense) bloom here in densities of 700,000 per gallon. Mechanical stress — a paddle, a fish, a raindrop — triggers a flash of light that scientists still don't fully understand.

title: Sahara Fertilises the Amazon
brief: 27 million tonnes of Sahara dust crosses the Atlantic yearly to feed the Amazon.
story: NASA's CALIPSO satellite tracks a river of phosphorus-rich dust blowing west from the Bodélé Depression in Chad. It replaces exactly the nutrients the Amazon loses to runoff. Two continents, one invisible supply chain.

title: Danakil Depression
brief: Hottest inhabited place on Earth. Lowest point in Africa. Alien chemistry.
story: 125 m below sea level. Year-round 34 °C average. Acid pools, salt pans, sulphur fumaroles — the closest Earth gets to Mars or Io. NASA uses it as a stand-in for extraterrestrial astrobiology tests.

title: Magnetic Hill
brief: Vehicles in neutral appear to roll uphill — an optical illusion that fools gravity itself.
story: The slope of the horizon tricks the eye. What looks uphill is actually a gentle downhill. Drivers report cars drifting 'up' at 20 km/h. ISRO imagery proves the surrounding terrain biases every visual cue.
